title: I/O: Parquet, ORC, CSV, JSON, text and Avro; Hadoop file systems; catalogs by configuration
verdict: data sources by `format`; `s3a://`, `abfss://`, `gs://` through Hadoop connectors; `spark.sql.catalog.*`
description: Spark reads and writes Parquet, ORC, CSV, JSON, text and binary files with its built-in sources, and Avro with the bundled `spark-avro` module. Object stores go through Hadoop's file system connectors (`s3a://`, `abfss://`, `gs://`), which need their jars and credentials in the Hadoop configuration (`spark.hadoop.*`). Catalogs other than the session's are plugins named by `spark.sql.catalog.<name>` (Iceberg's `SparkCatalog`, Delta's `DeltaCatalog`, Unity Catalog's), each from its own package. Parquet keeps `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` and `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` apart and stores decimals by precision.
reference: I/O is outside what a plan computes; sverify's `io` modules read and write the formats, and `sverify.spark_engine` hands Spark tables as temporary views.
